name: Values, appraisals, and closing the job
summary: The Values bar and the Closing bar mostly work as their own rules describe. I drove them through the real controls on the Ashworth probate estate (values tier, Formal, a co-representative), the Hale living Home Transition, a contents tier, a none tier, a Standard estate and a 450-line full house. My scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-app/107e11dc-7b83-525c-829c-97f2e5cca8f9/scratchpad/audit/VAL. For the concierge the flow is short: link an appraiser, type the report's figure in Total, press File the report once, and close from the desk with a few star presses and Close job. For the trust officer or the attorney, the papers are where it breaks. Three things reach a paper wrongly today. First, one select (Valuation Source: Appraisal, on the bulk bar or in the record) turns Agent Two's low-confidence $4,800 guess into an 'appraisal' on the Court Inventory, with no appraiser and no report. Second, on the Contents and None tiers the Release Approval Request prints a Fair Market Value basis, an 'Est. value' column of dashes footed '$0', and 'Values are Havellin's estimates', on engagements where Havellin is contracted not to value. Third, one inventory snapshot of a 450-line house makes the job record 68,124 characters. A Google Sheets cell holds 50,000, so every jobs write would fail, and the backend clears the Jobs tab before it writes. The FINAL rule on both schedules is weaker than the desk. It goes FINAL with signature lines while an appraisal the desk itself linked is still out (Standard estates), with an appraisal figure typed and no report on file, with unreviewed agent-named lines, and with red 'not stated' bases. The value date and the standard do not follow the job. The §2032 tick re-dates every header without touching a line, with no 706 gate, and the appraiser's packet still says 'date of death'. The basis select lets a §733.604 schedule be stated at Liquidation Value. Agent Two's 'Appraisal advised' is silenced by the review tick and never reaches the guardrail. The Appraisal Worklist leaves out lines the concierge linked to the appraiser, while the hand-off sheet includes them. Nothing compares what a line sold for with its value: a painting valued at $2,400 that sold for $9,000 raised nothing anywhere. No paper carries the comparables, range, confidence or reviewer behind a figure. Close job asks only about the midpoint and the ledger, while the desk shows undecided lines, approvals owed, an appraisal pending and proceeds with no statement. The biggest efficiency gains are agents reading the appraisal report and the auction settlement statement (today every figure is typed by hand), linking an appraiser across a selection, and signing the close-out papers on the iPad.
works_well: Linking an appraiser and typing the report's figure behaves as Q93 says. On Ashworth, typing $4,200 in the clock's Total recorded source Appraisal, valuedBy appraiser, valDate 2026-04-02 (the roster's effective date). The row read 'Appraisal · Carla Mendes … report not filed', and the Values bar flipped to '✓ nothing needs an appraisal · report not filed: Carla Mendes (1 item)' with no full redraw (v02-appraise.js).
File the report is one press. The file input in the roster cell filed a PDF as kind appraisal_report covering e07, and the row's and the bar's 'report not filed' both cleared at once (v02).
Changing the count on an appraised line never moves the appraisal: qty 2 left fmv at $4,200 and made Each $2,100 (v02).

Agent Two is told the estate's basis and valuation date ({estate:true, basis:'Fair Market Value', valuationDate:'2026-04-02', categories, conditions}). A general lot over the $250 ceiling went back for research in the same run (two agentValue calls for e20), as designed (v03b-net.js).

Where counsel values (contents tier), Agent Two's figure stays internal: fmv blank, the range $3,200–$7,500 on the row marked 'internal', the confirm says no document prints it, and the range still raises the appraisal flag for counsel (v05-contents-tier.js).

Proceeds statements reconcile exactly. Typing 'Kodner Galleries' ticked that vendor's two lines, the lot figures were written onto the lines, and the card read '✓ Agrees with the ledger'. The ledger then showed Gross $9,000 / Fees $2,250 / Net $6,750 for #1 (v03-values.js).
The Court Inventory's floor rule works: with unvalued lines it reads 'Total recorded so far … not a complete total' and names each missing line by number (v01).

An estate or a living job can be closed without leaving the desk: the star ratings sit in the Closing bar, Close job is in the band, and closing filed the Disposition Ledger (and the Contents Record on living work) through uploadHtml (v08-close.js).
Layout holds: zero horizontal overflow at 390 and 1024 px with Values, Closing and History open; the roster table scrolls inside .tbl-scroll (700/307 at 390) (v10-widths.js).

Removing an appraiser keeps a landed appraisal on its line with the appraiser named, and a report whose appraiser has left the roster stays listed with its Void (code: removeAppraiser havellin.html:36308, _renderAppraiserRoster:36560).
measurements: Job record size: 1,344 characters before an inventory snapshot and 68,124 after one snapshot of a 450-line probate house (151 characters per line), above Google Sheets' 50,000-character cell limit; the app then posted saveAllJobs at 68,159 bytes and job at 68,149 (v07-snapshot-size.js).

Close-out of the Ashworth estate from the desk: 3 star presses (one per vendor), then Close job, then one confirm. The confirm named 2 matters (no midpoint payment, ledger unsigned) while the desk carried 3 undecided lines, 3 items needing written approval, 1 appraisal pending on a Formal estate and 3 sold lines on no statement (v08-close.js estate).

Close-out of the Hale living job: 2 star presses, Close job, one confirm naming only the midpoint. Unmentioned: 2 undecided lines (the Contents Record's sign-off withheld) and a shotgun with no written authority (v08-close.js living).

Linking appraisers: one select per line, in the guardrail or the record's Appraisal Doc. The selection bar has no appraiser control (code: bulk menu havellin.html:40147-40170). 40 lines to one appraiser means 40 selects.
Recording an appraisal report covering N lines: N figures typed by hand plus 1 press of File the report (v02).

Proceeds dialog: each lot row is 173 px tall at 390 px against 41 px at 1024, inside a 240 px scroll box, so about 1.4 lots are visible at a time on a phone (v10-widths.js; screenshot out/v10-ps-390.png).
Values bar heading at rest on Ashworth: '1 needs an appraisal, each linked · 1 ready to hand to Carla Mendes (under Releases & signed papers) · 1 appraiser' (v01).

Same inventory, two papers: the Court Inventory went from 'DRAFT — 1 item pending appraisal' to 'FINAL' with 2 adoption lines once one figure was typed, while the Estate Inventory Report printed 'IN PROGRESS — 7 of 8 items reviewed' (v02).
verifier_note: The VAL report holds up. I reproduced 30 of its 31 findings myself, with my own browser scripts on the frozen copy (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-app/107e11dc-7b83-525c-829c-97f2e5cca8f9/scratchpad/audit/VAL-verify/x01 to x08) and by reading the code lines myself. Where the auditor injected an agent figure, I had the stubbed Agent Two write it through the real Value N lines press instead, and I drove every link, select, tick, typed figure and Waive through the real controls. VAL-25 is a duplicate of a known Open-work item. Where to adjust the report: (1) VAL-14 understates the close question, which also names rooms not cleared, leaving lines with nobody named and lines out with an appraiser; it omits exactly what VAL-14 lists. (2) VAL-01's wipe of the Jobs tab is reasoning: I measured the oversized job and the app posting it, and the cell cap is documented in main-sync.gs's own comment, but whether the Sheets clear lands when setValues throws is not observable here. (3) I rated several findings lower than the auditor, because the reported behaviour follows from a person's explicit choice that a recorded rule describes: VAL-02 (a source set to Appraisal takes the line outright, P23 §2.3), VAL-04 (on Standard the guardrail is advisory) and VAL-05 (Q93 makes File the report a flag). I also rated some new features lower (VAL-10, VAL-18). Proposals that touch a decided rule are named in their notes: VAL-02, VAL-05, VAL-07, VAL-15. New siblings I saw: under Liquidation Value the Court Inventory still heads its column 'FMV (total)' and its footer still says 'Values are estimated fair market value' (VAL-08); a desk figure typed over Agent Two's keeps the agent's stale range (VAL-07); the Formal guardrail reads '1 item need an appraisal' (VAL-25); and a vendor pickup is offered with no check that the line is linked to an appraiser or out with one (VAL-11).

findings.title: One inventory snapshot of a full house pushes the job past the Sheets cell limit; the backend clears the Jobs tab before writing
findings.where: History bar / More ▾ › Snapshot: takeInventorySnapshot havellin.html:30265 (_snapItemOf:30261 stores every line in job.invSnapshots); backend saveAllJobsToSheet apps-script/main-sync.gs:1520-1521 (clearContent, then setValues of JSON.stringify(job) in one cell); single upsert :1574
findings.evidence: Measured: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-app/107e11dc-7b83-525c-829c-97f2e5cca8f9/scratchpad/audit/VAL/v07-snapshot-size.js seeded a 450-line probate house and pressed More ▾ › Snapshot. It printed 'job JSON chars before snapshot: 1344 | after one snapshot: {len:68124, snaps:1, items:450}' and the app posted 'saveAllJobs:68159', 'job:68149'. Reasoning, not observed: Google Sheets refuses more than 50,000 characters in one cell, and the Jobs tab stores each job as one JSON cell (column L). saveAllJobsToSheet rewrites every job's row in one setValues after clearing the rows (main-sync.gs:1520-1521). So the write throws for every job on every device, and the outbox retries forever. If the clear has already landed when setValues throws, the Jobs tab is empty. JobLedger then reads every job id as seen-and-absent, refuses it as 'deleted', and _applyDroppedJobs (havellin.html:42162) drops it on the device.
findings.tc_impact: The concierge presses Snapshot once ('As of date of death') and, at best, every client's edits stop syncing with a stuck chip. At worst every job is wiped. The attorney's 'filed with court' trail is the trigger.
findings.proposal: Move snapshot items out of the job record. Keep {ts, label, valueDate, count, totalFMV, voided…} on job.invSnapshots and store the lines in the MediaStore entry (or a store of their own, chunked like EstimateStore). Better still, file the snapshot as the rendered Court Inventory or Estate Inventory Report PDF to Drive and keep the link. In saveAllJobsToSheet, build every row and check each JSON against 50,000 characters before clearContent; refuse the oversized job by name and never clear first. Add a test that a 600-line snapshot leaves the job under 40,000 characters. Ship it with a BACKEND_VERSION bump and a redeploy note.
findings.vnote: I seeded a full probate house with short, realistic names and pressed More ▾ › Snapshot through the real menu. 330 lines made the job 44,840 characters (132 per line). 420 lines made it about 56,700, and the app then posted saveAllJobs at 56,771 bytes and job at 56,761. So one snapshot passes 50,000 characters at about 380 lines, two at about 190, before the job's own docState, approvals and records are counted. A full house is 200 to 600 lines. The Jobs tab keeps each job as one JSON cell (column L) with no chunking: saveAllJobsToSheet (main-sync.gs:1477-1530) runs clearContent and then setValues, and saveJobToSheet (:1534-1580) writes a single row. The backend's own comment at main-sync.gs:615 says setValue throws above 50,000 characters, which is why the stores are chunked and the Jobs tab is not. Every saveAllJobs from a device that holds the job therefore fails and retries forever. That the clear can land before the throw and leave the Jobs tab empty, so the ledger reads every job as deleted, is reasoning: it cannot be observed here.

findings.title: Setting Valuation Source to 'Appraisal' turns Agent Two's guess into an appraisal on the court schedule
findings.where: Selection bar › Set valuation source… (havellin.html:40151 → _invBulkApply:37368 → _avTakeValue(ref,'appraisal') :38752); the record's Valuation Source select through _invEdit:29776
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-app/107e11dc-7b83-525c-829c-97f2e5cca8f9/scratchpad/audit/VAL/v09-bulk-appraisal.js: an agent-valued painting (fmv 4800, range 3200–7500, confidence low, 'Online comps', flagged for appraisal by its range). I ticked its row and picked Appraisal on the bar. There was no dialog. The line became {fmv:4800, src:'Appraisal', by:'appraiser'} with the range, confidence and basis sentence deleted and no apprId. The Values bar went from '2 need an appraisal' to '1 needs an appraisal'. The Court Inventory printed '| Oil on canvas still life, signed lower left | as photographed | appraisal | $4,800' and the Estate Inventory Report 'Appraisal'.
findings.tc_impact: One stray select on 40 picked lines makes 40 AI estimates read as appraisals and clears the Formal guardrail. The attorney receives 'appraisal' beside a figure no appraiser made, with nobody named and no report in Drive. It is the most indefensible line a schedule can carry.
findings.proposal: Keep 'Appraisal' as a source only where the appraisal's figure is written: drop it from the bulk menu, and on the record allow it only once an appraiser is linked (or counsel's appraiser is named in a box). The figure must be typed after the choice, so _avTakeValue's 'appraisal' arm never adopts an existing valuedBy 'agent' figure. Over an agent figure, ask: 'This value is Agent Two's estimate. Type the appraiser's figure to record it as the appraisal.' invValBasisWord should print 'appraisal (appraiser not named)' where no appraiser is recorded.
findings.decided_conflict: P25 Q36: appraised = source Appraisal with a value, linked or not (counsel's appraiser). The proposal keeps that case but requires the figure to be the appraisal's own, typed after the choice.
findings.vnote: The stubbed Agent Two valued #40 through the real Value 4 lines press (fmv 4800, range 3200–7500, confidence low, Online comps), and the Values bar read '2 need an appraisal'. I ticked #40's row and picked Appraisal in the bar's 'Set valuation source…' select. No dialog appeared. The line became {fmv:4800, src:'Appraisal', by:'appraiser'} with the range, confidence and note gone and no apprId. The bar dropped to '1 needs an appraisal'. The Court Inventory printed '| Oil on canvas still life, signed lower left | Good | appraisal | $4,800', and the Estate Inventory Report printed 'Appraisal'. The code is _invBulkApply:37368 → _avTakeValue('appraisal') at :38752, and the record's select takes the same path (:29758). Re-rated high rather than fix-now: it takes a person's explicit select, and the decided ownership rule (P23 §2.3 and Q36: a source set to Appraisal takes the line outright) says that is what the select means. The proposal should keep that rule and only ask first when the figure on the line is Agent Two's, or leave Appraisal off the bulk menu.

Filing the report clears both. Offer File the report in the guardrail row as the figure lands.
findings.decided_conflict: Q93 (2026-10-24): File the report is a flag, never a block. The proposal leaves the desk unblocked and only makes the paper say a report is owed; whether that holds FINAL is Anthony's call.

findings.title: A figure the concierge types over Agent Two's prints 'not stated' in red, and FINAL ignores it
findings.where: _avTakeValue havellin.html:38768 (typed over the agent drops valSource and valNote); INV_VAL_SOURCES :28235 has no desk source; Court Inventory basis column _invScheduleSection :33996; the FINAL rule does not check basis
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-app/107e11dc-7b83-525c-829c-97f2e5cca8f9/scratchpad/audit/VAL/v03-values.js: after Agent Two valued the copper cookware at $40 ('General estimate'), I typed 300 in its Total. The line became {fmv:300, by:'desk'} with no source, and the Court Inventory printed '| Copper cookware set | Good | not stated | $300' in red. v11-standard-pending.js printed FINAL with two adoption lines over the clock's '$3,500 | not stated'. No row control names a source; the Valuation Source select is inside each line's record.
findings.tc_impact: Anthony's own model is 'if I see something off on the desk review, I'll change it'. Every correction then reads as a figure with no basis on the schedule counsel signs, unless the concierge opens each record and picks a source that does not describe them ('PR estimate' is the representative's).
findings.proposal: Add a desk source to INV_VAL_SOURCES, 'Havellin estimate (reviewed)' (schedule word 'Havellin estimate'), and let a typed figure default to it, with valReviewedBy kept as who typed it. Better still, keep Agent Two's comparables when the typed figure sits inside the agent's range. Make the FINAL rule list 'N valued lines with no basis stated' among its draft reasons on Formal.
findings.decided_conflict: Job-flow audit rule (2026-10-08): a figure the desk types over the agent's drops the agent's source and sentence, so the line reads 'not stated' until the desk names one. The proposal keeps dropping the agent's source but names the desk's instead of leaving it blank.
findings.vnote: Agent Two valued #23 at $40 (General estimate). I typed 300 in its Total. The line became {fmv:300, by:'desk'} with no source, and the Court Inventory printed '| Copper cookware set | Good | not stated | $300'. In x03, both Formal and Standard schedules went FINAL with four 'not stated' bases in red, so the FINAL rule never reads the basis. Sibling: the typed line keeps the agent's stale range (valLow 30, valHigh 50) under a $300 desk figure. findings.tc_impact: Months later, counsel asks what the filed schedule said and on what basis, and the snapshot can answer only names and numbers.
findings.proposal: When a snapshot is taken, file the rendered Court Inventory or Estate Inventory Report (asHtml → PDF) to Drive under a dated name. Keep a compact diff record (adding qty, valSource, valDate, apprId) outside the job cell (see VAL-01). Make Compare show source and count changes.
